headline: Earnings dip, guidance holds, new outlook introduced

kpis.label: Net income attributable to CMS Energy

summary_short: CMS Energy's Q2 2026 diluted EPS fell to $0.37 from $0.66 a year ago on revenue of $1.83B (-0.5% y/y), with adjusted EPS down to $0.37 from $0.71. The company reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.83-$3.90 and introduced FY2027 guidance of $4.08-$4.17.
summary_long: Revenue was roughly flat y/y at $1.83B, but operating income fell 16.7% and net income attributable to CMS Energy dropped to $120M from $201M, pulling diluted EPS to $0.37 from $0.66 and adjusted EPS to $0.37 from $0.71; the release does not explain the y/y decline at the company or segment level. CMS completed a strategic review of NorthStar Clean Energy, exiting non-utility renewables development while retaining Michigan-based assets including Dearborn Industrial Generation, to simplify the business and cut financing needs. CMS reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $3.83-$3.90 with confidence toward the high end, and introduced FY2027 guidance of $4.08-$4.17. Cash fell to $241M from $844M y/y; long-term debt rose to $18.17B.

drivers.explanation: Company completed a strategic review and is exiting non-utility renewables development at NorthStar Clean Energy (retaining Michigan-based DIG asset) to simplify the business and cut financing needs; reaffirmed 2026 guidance and introduced 2027 guidance despite the Q2 EPS decline.

drivers.metric: Net income attributable to CMS Energy
drivers.explanation: Decline roughly tracks the drop in operating income (-16.7% y/y) plus a larger noncontrolling-interest loss ($24M vs $8M a year ago); the release breaks out neither by segment.
